expected_non_findings.rationale: Accepting '^' as negation is the intended feature.

files.patch:
@@ -140,12 +140,14 @@
             if end == -1:
                 raise UnsafePathError("glob has an unterminated character class")
             body = segment[i + 1 : end]
-            negate = body.startswith("!")
+            # gitignore accepts both "[!...]" and the regex-style "[^...]" for negation.
+            negate = body[:1] in ("!", "^")
             if negate:
                 body = body[1:]
+            if not body:
+                raise UnsafePathError("glob has an empty character class")
             body = body.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("^", "\\^")
             out += f"[{'^' if negate else ''}{body}]"
-            i = end
         else:
             out += re.escape(ch)
         i += 1

pull_request.body: gitignore users expect `[^abc]` to work like `[!abc]`. Also reject empty classes.
pull_request.title: Support [^...] negated character classes in globs

ground_truth.rationale: The 'i = end' line was removed, so after emitting the class the loop continues inside it and re-emits its characters and the closing bracket as literals: '*.[ch]' no longer matches 'a.c'. Include/exclude globs with classes silently break.
